wrong_fix_catalogue.wrong_resource: n/a: the task protects the TLS session to the vCenter named in the request, not a resource chosen by an identity field, so there is no neighbouring object an authorisation check could pick
wrong_fix_catalogue.one_role_or_direction: n/a: the agent is always the TLS client; there is no peer role or opposite direction to fix separately
wrong_fix_catalogue.check_after_adjustment: n/a: the decision is a flag and a bundle carried with the credentials; there is no path or value normalisation between the request and the TLS handshake that could turn a validated value into a different one
wrong_fix_catalogue.malformed_identity: n/a: no name or identifier parsing decides the guard; the bundle is parsed by the TLS stack itself and an unusable bundle is rejected before connecting
wrong_fix_catalogue.missing_authority: n/a: there is no authority lookup that could fail open; an absent bundle has a defined meaning (skip by default, system roots on an explicit false) rather than a missing permission

traps.realistic_because: the reported hardcoded insecure parameter is exactly here; a solver that treats the shared constructor as the whole fix leaves the options unread
the forecaster duplicates the credential check with its own SOAP client instead of the shared helper; a solver who rewires the shared helpers can leave this copy hardcoded

traps.shape: route where the protection never existed (documented risk acceptance)
traps.realistic_because: a separate package opens its own connection from a config builder that documents skip-verify as a deliberate, reasoned risk acceptance, so it reads as out of scope and by design
the validation-only preflight logs in and out and looks like a credential check rather than an operational connection, so it is easy to leave out of the transport fix

traps.shape: shape trap: explicit false in a tri-state option
traps.realistic_because: the option has three states (absent, false, true) and the safest-looking reading of an absent bundle is to skip; a mapper that collapses absent and false onto skip passes every check about bundles but silently ignores an explicit request to validate

traps.shape: injected sibling: raw TLS reachability probe
traps.realistic_because: a maintainer-added fail-fast reachability dial before the inventory pipeline; it reads as plumbing, opens its own TLS session, and sits in a package and a file the published fix never touches

traps.shape: injected sibling: second transport (REST metadata client)
traps.realistic_because: a best-effort vCenter REST metadata query that opens a plain HTTPS client rather than a SOAP client; a solver fixing the SOAP transport never sees it, and errors are ignored so it looks harmless
